chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Muhammad, both, from Ali ibn al-Hasan-Hasan al-Taymi, from Muhammad ibn al-Khatab al-Wasiti, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Halbi, from Hammad al-Azdi, from Hisham al-Khaffaf, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'How is your insight into the stars?' I said: 'I left in Iraq no one with more insight into the stars than I.' He said: 'How is the rotation of the celestial sphere with you?' I took my cap from my head and rotated it. He said: 'If the matter is as you say, then what of Banat al-Na'sh, Al-Jady, and Al-Farqadayn? They are not seen to rotate in a day from the time in the direction [of the Qibla]?' I said: 'By Allah, this is something I do not know, and I did not hear anyone from the people of calculation mention it.' He said to me: 'What is the proportion of light of Al-Sukayna from Al-Zuhra?' I said: 'By Allah, this is a star I have not heard of, nor did I hear anyone from the people mention it.' He said: 'Glory be to Allah! So you have dropped a whole star, so upon what do you base your calculation?'

Then he said: 'So what is the proportion of illumination of Al-Zuhra from the moon?' I said: 'This is something only Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows.' He said: 'So what is the proportion of the moon from the sun in its illumination?' I said: 'I do not know this.' He said: 'You speak the truth.' Then he said: 'So what about the two armies meeting each other? In this one, a calculator [says victory], and in that one, a calculator [says victory]. This one calculates victory for his master, and that one calculates victory for his master. Then they meet, and one defeats the other. So where were the bad omens?' I said: 'By Allah, I do not know that.' He said: 'You speak the truth. The origin of calculation is true, but no one knows that except the one who knows the births of all creation.'

key_terms.بَنَاتِ النَّعْشِ: Banat al-Na'sh (a constellation, part of Ursa Major)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia view on astrology and the stars according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) engages a knowledgeable astrologer to demonstrate the limitations of human calculation by questioning specific stellar movements and magnitudes, such as the unseen 'Banat al-Na’sh' and the ratio of Venus to the Moon. He concludes that while the mathematical basis of astrology may hold some truth, its predictive power is flawed because only Allah possesses the comprehensive knowledge of the 'births' (mawālid) of all creation, thereby distinguishing between mere calculation and divine omniscience.
